long_biography.plain_text:
Sergio Galeotti persuaded Giorgio Armani to exchange a secure design career for their own Milan fashion house. The pair equipped its first office with proceeds from Armani's Volkswagen Beetle, with Galeotti directing the finances while Armani created the clothes. His unstructured jackets loosened traditional tailoring, and Richard Gere's wardrobe in American Gigolo carried the look to an international audience.

After Galeotti died, Armani chose not to sell and assumed control of both design and the business. He kept the group private while extending the name across clothing, accessories and interiors. He created a foundation and binding succession plan to preserve the company's creative identity, while instructing his heirs to pursue a partial sale or eventual flotation.
long_biography.html:
Sergio Galeotti persuaded Giorgio Armani to exchange a secure design career for their own Milan fashion house. The pair equipped its first office with proceeds from Armani's Volkswagen Beetle, with Galeotti directing the finances while Armani created the clothes. His unstructured jackets loosened traditional tailoring, and Richard Gere's wardrobe in American Gigolo carried the look to an international audience.

After Galeotti died, Armani chose not to sell and assumed control of both design and the business. He kept the group private while extending the name across clothing, accessories and interiors. He created a foundation and binding succession plan to preserve the company's creative identity, while instructing his heirs to pursue a partial sale or eventual flotation.
